title: Axolotl Collective
text:
Axolotl Collective

notes:
Founders: ex-game-dev + solo ML engineer. indie dev / micro-startup vibe.
Signed up through product landing page after reading benchmark blog post (low friction).
Primary MVP: a lightweight in-editor code helper for microservices — uses chat + code-assist flows.
Requirements summary: latency 150-250ms p95 for short completions (<=80 tokens), throughput modest (20-40 reqs/min), cost-sensitive (working on freemium to $50/mo paying users first).
Prefer US public cloud region (us-east), no need for VPC or on-prem yet. Wants simple API key management and an easy SDK for Rust/node.
Model preferences: open models or verified performant variants; interested in quantized options if cost savings do not blow up latency.
Routing/fallback: would like automatic fallback to smaller model when quota hit — asked if Redwood supports variant routing out of the box.
Security: basic SSO later when team >5; for now wants audit logs and API key rotation support. Quote from founder: "we just need predictable spend and fast ramp — billing is the hold-up".
Trial behavior: tried embeddings pipeline and saw ~3x cost vs expected due to naive batching; asked for docs/examples on batching + prefix caching.
Support requests: asked via in-product chat for recommended batch size and example caching config for small documents (response sent with link to docs).
Next product ask: short QA guide showing typical token budgets for chat vs code-assist so they can model pricing into freemium plans.
Sales motion: currently PLG only — no AE outreach yet. Recommend soft-touch nurture: automated onboarding sequence + example repo (rust + node) and invite to community Slack.
Potential upsell: when they reach $200/mo or require team SSO, convert to AE-assisted Dedicated discussion.

timeline:
2026-03-01: created account, signed up via self-serve (free credits)
2026-03-03: first test call against hosted API (simple chat prompt, 50 tokens)
2026-03-05: short sync with product ops (Fireflies ff_2026_03_05_9274) — discussed latency expectations and token billing
2026-03-07: uploaded small embeddings dataset (~2k docs), noticed higher-than-expected cost in naive batch test
2026-03-10: sandboxed prototypes running (backend in Rust) — reported occasional 200-300ms tail latencies for single-shot completions

blockers:
unclear cost projection for high token volumes
want low-latency in us-east region
need simple billing + team seats

next_step:
Monitor product usage; send onboarding tips email and invite to weekly PLG office hours; check back if trial spend > $50/mo
